summary: Joined node1, node2, and node3 into a single RabbitMQ 4.3.5 cluster (Erlang 27) on RHEL10, created the `payments` vhost with a durable quorum queue `payments.orders` (exchange `payments.events`, routing key `orders`) replicated across all 3 nodes, and an `app_user` account scoped to that vhost that can publish and consume. Verified messages published to the durable queue survive the loss of a node and remain consumable from the surviving nodes. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time OS reboot protocol on all three nodes, confirming changed boot identity and full cluster/data recovery after each.
actions_performed: Installed Erlang 27 and RabbitMQ 4.3.5 from official RabbitMQ el9 yum repos on all three RHEL10 nodes
Fixed an OpenSSL ABI mismatch (erlang crypto NIF needed OpenSSL 3.4+ symbols not present in RHEL10 GA's 3.2.2) by updating openssl-libs to 3.5.5 on all nodes
Opened firewalld ports 4369, 25672, 5672, 15672, 35672-35682 on all nodes for clustering/AMQP/management traffic
Propagated the actual runtime Erlang cookie (/var/lib/rabbitmq/.erlang.cookie) from node1 to node2 and node3 via SSH using the cluster keypair
Joined node2 and node3 to node1 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster; enabled rabbitmq_management plugin cluster-wide
Created the payments vhost and an app_user account (random password generated and stored only on managed nodes, never exposed in commands or this report) with full permissions on that vhost
Declared durable exchange payments.events, durable quorum queue payments.orders (replicated to all 3 nodes), and bound them with routing key orders
Captured a healthy baseline: 3/3 nodes running, quorum queue with all 3 members

Published a durable message, stopped the queue leader node's rabbitmq-server to simulate node loss while preserving quorum, confirmed leader failover, published a second message during the outage, and consumed both messages from a surviving node
Restarted the stopped node's rabbitmq-server and confirmed full cluster/queue recovery
Captured pre-reboot boot IDs and service health on all 3 nodes
Rebooted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially (one at a time) via systemctl reboot, polling each until reachable again
Verified each node's boot_id changed after reboot, proving an actual OS restart occurred
After each node's reboot, verified rabbitmq-server active, all 3 nodes back in cluster, and quorum queue healthy before proceeding to the next node
Ran a final end-to-end publish/consume test across nodes after all reboots to confirm full functionality

evidence.requirement: Cluster formed from node1, node2, node3
evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl join_cluster succeeded for node2 and node3; cluster_status from node1 shows all 3 nodes as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes
rabbitmqctl add_vhost payments and list_vhosts confirms payments vhost exists

evidence.requirement: Application account can publish and consume in payments vhost
evidence.summary: app_user created with permissions on payments vhost; successfully declared topology and published/consumed messages using app_user credentials

evidence.requirement: Durable queue survives loss of one node and stays consumable from remaining nodes
evidence.summary: Baseline: quorum queue with 1 msg, 3 members. Stopped leader node1's rabbitmq-server (node down). Cluster status from node2 showed leader failover to node2 with message count preserved at 1. Published a second message during the outage (count became 2). Consumed both messages successfully from node3 while node1 was still down. Restarted node1 and confirmed full 3-node cluster recovery.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline, reboot ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-reboot boot_id 2b19e976-... captured with rabbitmq-server active. systemctl reboot acknowledged before disconnect. Post-reboot boot_id dbcffc19-... (changed). rabbitmq-server active again, all 3 nodes running, quorum queue with 3 members restored.

evidence.requirement: Node2 restart: healthy baseline, reboot ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-reboot boot_id 73237116-... captured with rabbitmq-server active. Reboot acknowledged before disconnect. Post-reboot boot_id 625feaa1-... (changed). rabbitmq-server active again, all 3 nodes running, quorum queue with 3 members restored.

evidence.requirement: Node3 restart: healthy baseline, reboot ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-reboot boot_id 434803ac-... captured with rabbitmq-server active. Reboot acknowledged before disconnect. Post-reboot boot_id 7b2c5d5a-... (changed). rabbitmq-server active again, all 3 nodes running, quorum queue with 3 members restored.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart functional verification of full pipeline
evidence.summary: After all three reboots, published a message via node1 using app_user, confirmed it landed in the durable quorum queue, consumed it successfully from node2, and confirmed final user/permission/cluster state.
